items.title: Validation badges on the sequence header are not clickable, so the only way to read '1 error' is to press Start
items.reasoning: The claim is in the code and is complete. support_widgets.dart:610-618 wraps the badge Row in Tooltip('Show sequence issues') + InkWell(onTap: SequenceIssuesDialog.show), and sequence_issues_dialog.dart reads the SAME ref.watch(liveValidationProvider).issues that feeds the header counts (sequence_tree.dart:319 -> sequence_header.dart:117-124), so the dialog cannot list a different set from what the badge counted. Issues are sorted error->warning->info, each row shows title + description + resolutionHint, and rows with affectedNodeId set selectedNodeIdProvider and pop. I checked for other badge surfaces: grep for errorCount/liveValidationProvider across skotiq_app shows only this header, the pre-flight dialog (which already listed issues) and sequence_mutator_helper's force-save dialog, so there is no second inert copy. The badge is width-gated at constraints.maxWidth > 320 rather than device class, so it is reachable on a phone too. The deliberately-skipped half (reclassifying Empty Sequence / No Exposures from error to info) is correctly skipped: both genuinely block Start (they are hard errors in the pre-flight gate), so downgrading them would have been an INVERTED fix.
items.evidence: SEVER TEST DONE: replaced `onTap: () => SequenceIssuesDialog.show(context)` with `onTap: null` in support_widgets.dart:617 and re-ran packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/validation_badge_opens_issues_test.dart - RED ('Found 0 widgets with type SequenceIssuesDialog'). Restored the line and re-ran - 1/1 green. The test drives the real SequenceTree with a real CurrentSequenceNotifier and asserts every live issue title appears, so it binds to production wiring rather than a fixture.

items.title: Live Stacking's explanatory helper text is truncated to one ellipsised line
items.reasoning: The diagnosis and the fix are both real. packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/theme/skotiq_theme.dart:231 now sets helperMaxLines: 4 inside the one InputDecorationTheme in the whole repo (grep for 'InputDecorationTheme(' returns exactly that line), and it sits inside SkotiqTheme._buildTheme, which is the single body behind dark/light/redNight/darkWithAccent/lightWithAccent AND behind resolveSkotiqThemeData, which is what apps/mobile/lib/main.dart:415,496 uses - so mobile is covered too, not just desktop. I checked the overflow risk the fixer waved away: the widest-blast-radius call site outside the sequencer is guiding_panel.dart's _ConfigInputRow, whose helper sits in an unconstrained Column inside a Row with crossAxisAlignment.start, so a 2-3 line helper grows the row rather than overflowing it. The skotiq_ui suite is green with the change in.
items.evidence: SEVER TEST DONE: deleted the `helperMaxLines: 4,` line from skotiq_theme.dart and re-ran packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/live_stacking_helper_wrap_test.dart - BOTH tests went red (maxLines null; RenderParagraph.didExceedMaxLines true). Restored, re-ran - 2/2 green. The test renders the real LiveStackingProperties at 360 px and asserts on the rendered RenderParagraph, so it binds to the shipped theme rather than to a constructed InputDecoration. REGRESSION CHECK: full skotiq_ui suite run with the change in place - exit 0.

items.title: Two different things are called Save, two different things are called Templates, and the tab names collide
items.reasoning: Both halves of the claimed edit are genuinely in the tree and both are covered: sequence_toolbar.dart:510-522 labels the floppy 'Export Sequence File…' (and the disabled variant), line 401 passes operationName: 'Export Sequence File' to the force-save dialog, and snippet_palette/rendering.dart:45 and :160 (wide and compact headers) plus the :325 'Search snippets...' hint all say snippet. The top-level Templates tab (sequencer_screen.dart:59) is now the only thing in the sequencer called Templates, so the collision is genuinely gone from the labels. What the fixer missed is the SAME collision on the export function's own failure and success paths, four lines from the operationName they did change: the catch blocks said 'Failed to save sequence: $e' (twice) and revealExportedFile's desktopMessage said 'Sequence "X" saved' / '"X" saved (forced)'. So you press a button that says Export, it fails, and the app tells you a SAVE failed - which is precisely the ambiguity the finding is about, on the path where it matters most. Worse, the Exposure Triggers snackbar still ended '— save sequence to persist.', pointing the operator at a 'save' that, after this rename, no longer exists in the toolbar and never persisted into the library anyway (the floppy exports a .nsq). The button label was fixed; the sentences around it were not.
items.evidence: SEVER TESTS DONE, three. (a) Toolbar: replaced the label with 'Save Sequence' -> naming_collisions_test 'the toolbar file action does not call itself Save' RED; restored -> green. (b) Snippets: replaced both 'Snippets' header strings with 'Templates' -> 'the snippets panel calls itself Snippets' RED; restored -> green. (c) My repair: reverted 'Failed to export sequence file: $e' to 'Failed to save sequence: $e' -> my new test RED ('Found 0 widgets with text containing Failed to export'); restored -> 3/3 green. My test drives the real SequenceToolbar with sequenceFileServiceProvider overridden by a SequenceFileService subclass whose exportSequence throws, so it exercises the production catch block rather than the string constant.
items.repairSummary: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/sequence_toolbar.dart: both export catch blocks now say 'Failed to export sequence file: …', the two revealExportedFile desktopMessages say 'exported' / 'exported (forced)' instead of 'saved', and the exposure-trigger snackbar now says 'use "Save Current" in the Sequences tab to persist.' instead of the ambiguous 'save sequence to persist.' (the stale comment above it, which claimed the toolbar's Save persists, was corrected too). Added 'the file action reports failure as an export, not a save' to packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/naming_collisions_test.dart, which fails if the copy is reverted.

items.title: Filter is a free-text field with no binding to the wheel; a typo becomes a 2am run failure
items.reasoning: The fixer's two factual claims are both true. The Change Filter editor really is a profile-bound DropdownButton with a '(not in profile)' sentinel row (_capture_rich.dart:106-160, _kMissingFilterSentinel), and so is the Exposure editor (_exposure_rich.dart:517-560) - the 'plain text box' only appears when the profile declares no filters at all. FilterInWheelRule really does bail unless the wheel is connected (filter_rules.dart:41-45). The new FilterInProfileRule (filter_rules.dart:100-137) is correct in substance: case-insensitive, silent on an empty/absent profile, silent when a wheel is connected, walks the shared _filterUses helper so it and FilterInWheelRule cover the same two node types, and it IS registered in defaultRefAwareSequenceValidators (sequence_validation.dart:355), which is the list liveValidationProvider builds its service from (live_validation_provider.dart:171-177). What is missing is on the other side of the loop. LiveValidationNotifier listens to the sequence, six device-state slices and appSettings - but NOT to the equipment profile, which this fix has just made a first-class validation input. activeEquipmentProfileProvider derives from equipmentProfilesProvider (profiles_provider.dart:1147-1150), which nothing in that listen list reaches. So the operator reads 'Exposure "Lights" uses filter "Ha", which the active equipment profile does not list', goes to Equipment, adds Ha, comes back - and the badge still says it, until a device connects or they touch the sequence. A new rule that keeps accusing you after you have complied is the repo's own cry-wolf class. Separately, and NOT repaired because it is a different defect: CenterNode's 'Solve Filter' (_motion_rich.dart:140-153) genuinely IS a free-text filter box, and it is not covered by _filterUses - but validating it would be theatre, because execute_center (instructions.rs:1533-1830) never reads CenterConfig.filter at all. That field is a dead control, which is a separate finding, not this one.
items.evidence: SEVER TESTS DONE, three. (a) The shipped test binds NOTHING: I deleted `FilterInProfileRule(),` from defaultRefAwareSequenceValidators and packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/rules/filter_in_profile_rule_test.dart stayed 7/7 GREEN - it constructs the rule directly, so the whole production registration was deletable with the suite green. (b) With my new skotiq_app test in place, the same deletion turns it RED ('FilterInProfileRule is not registered in the live rule stack'); restored -> green. (c) Deleting my new activeEquipmentProfileProvider listen turns the second new test RED while the first stays green, which is exactly the staleness this repair closes; restored -> 2/2 green. REGRESSION CHECK: skotiq_core test/providers/sequence/ 514/514 green with both edits in.
items.repairSummary: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/live_validation_provider.dart now listens to activeEquipmentProfileProvider (import of profiles_provider.dart added), so editing or switching the equipment profile re-runs live validation and the 'Filter Not in Profile' warning clears when the operator fixes it - this also fixes the same staleness for the pre-existing SmartExposureFilterNotInProfileRule. Added packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/filter_profile_validation_wiring_test.dart, which drives the real liveValidationProvider: test 1 fails if the rule is unregistered, test 2 fails if the profile listen is removed.

items.title: Loop defaults to 1 iteration and Conditional defaults to 'Always Execute' - both are no-ops out of the box
items.reasoning: The code is exactly as described and it is wired: NoOpLogicNodeRule (logic_node_rules.dart:412-461) flags a count-mode Loop at <=1 and a Conditional set to always, at INFO, with affectedNodeId, and it is registered in defaultSequenceValidators (sequence_validation.dart:323) which liveValidationProvider passes as syncRules (live_validation_provider.dart:169). INFO really does surface: _NodeValidationWrapper paints an info badge on the node (support_widgets.dart:512-522), _ValidationBadges renders infoCount (support_widgets.dart:636-640) and SequenceIssuesDialog lists info issues (sequence_issues_dialog.dart:32). I also checked for cry-wolf on the app's own content: every bundled template Loop is forever/whileDark or an explicit count (10/20/100/5), and every bundled Conditional is weatherSafe or altitudeAbove 30, so nothing shipped trips the new rule, and the quick-start wizard uses the operator's own _loopCount. So the rule is correct and quiet. BUT the finding was a wrong-DEFAULT complaint ('both are no-ops out of the box') and the fix changes no default - it adds a message saying so. That is disclosure by this campaign's own definition. It is weaker than the summary claims, too: the fixer's justification rests on 'the tree shows no sign of it', which is false. node_summary.dart:502-523 already rendered the Loop row as an inline-editable '× 1' fragment and the Conditional row as 'if always' - the state was on the row, and the loop count was editable in place. The new badge therefore adds emphasis, not information. I did NOT repair by picking a default: the fixer's argument that 2-vs-10 is unknowable is sound, ConditionalType has no unset member (simple_logic_nodes.dart:168, every other member needs a threshold), and inventing one here would impose taste on every sequence built from the palette. This needs an owner decision on node_palette.dart:444/450, not a verifier's guess.
items.evidence: SEVER TEST DONE: commented out `NoOpLogicNodeRule(),` at sequence_validation.dart:323 and re-ran packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/rules/no_op_logic_node_rule_test.dart - RED on 'the rule is wired into the default validator set' (6 pass, 1 fail); restored the line and re-ran - 7/7 green. That last test calls the production validateSequence() over defaultSequenceValidators, so the shipped test does bind the registration (unlike the FilterInProfileRule test in item 4, which did not). Premise check: sed of node_summary.dart:500-523 shows _loopSummary emitting StaticFragment('×') + EditableFragment(loopIterations, '${repeatCount ?? 1}') and _conditionalDescriptor returning 'always', i.e. the tree row already displayed both no-op states.

items.title: Mosaic preview shows only 5 of 9 panel numbers for a 3x3 grid and hides the centre panel's number under the drag handle
items.reasoning: The edit is real - visual_planner.dart moves the number out of Center() into a top-left corner badge with a black 0.55 scrim, and the handle carries ValueKey('mosaic_center_handle') - and the 'only 5 of 9 render' half really is not reproducible. But the load-bearing claim, 'it clears the handle for EVERY GRID PARITY', is false, and the fixer only asserted it for the default 3x3. An odd grid puts the handle in the MIDDLE of a cell, which a top-left badge clears. An EVEN grid puts the handle on the shared CORNER of four cells - which is exactly where a top-left badge lives - so the collision comes straight back on 2x2 / 4x4. I measured it on the real dialog: at 2x2 the handle rect is (964.0,496.0,976.0,508.0) and panel 2's number rect is (971.3,502.6,988.6,528.6) - a genuine overlap, and because the handle is the LAST child of the planner Stack it paints on top of the digit. It also gets worse as overlap % rises: the right column's left edge sits at centerX - panelWidth*overlap/2, so a bigger overlap drags the badge further under the handle. The defect did not go away, it moved from odd grids to even ones. (Panel geometry is the only thing I could check; how legible the badge is against a real HiPS background is a look-at-it question, not a test one.)
items.evidence: MEASURED, not inferred: a scratch probe over the real MosaicWizardDialog drove the Columns and Rows steppers from 3 to 2 and printed every label rect against the handle rect - 'label 2: Rect.fromLTRB(971.3, 502.6, 988.6, 528.6) overlapsHandle=true'. (An earlier form of the assertion surfaced as the binding's '_pendingExceptionDetails != null' assert rather than a clean failure, because the shared _pumpMosaic helper overrides FlutterError.onError to swallow overflow - worth knowing for anyone else editing that file.) SEVER TEST DONE on my repair: moved the new number layer back to BEFORE the handle in the Stack and re-ran mosaic_panel_labels_test - RED on 'an EVEN grid still wins the z-order against the centre handle'; restored - 4/4 green. REGRESSION CHECK: all five mosaic wizard test files (mosaic_panel_labels, mosaic_wizard_visual, mosaic_wizard_create_project, mosaic_wizard_resume, mosaic_wizard_exposure) 23/23 green with the repair in.
items.repairSummary: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/mosaic_wizard_dialog/visual_planner.dart: the panel numbers are now their own IgnorePointer layer (_panelNumber) drawn AFTER the centre handle instead of living inside each panel's Container, with the cell geometry extracted into a shared _panelGeometry helper so body and badge cannot drift. No corner placement clears the handle for both grid parities, so the digit wins the z-order - it is the information that maps the picture onto the plan's panel numbers, and the handle is still readable as a dot behind it. The badge keeps a ValueKey('mosaic_panel_number_<row>_<col>') so paint order is assertable, and taps still fall through to the panel's GestureDetector. Rewrote the even-grid case in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/widgets/mosaic_panel_labels_test.dart to assert that order (it also fails if the numbers move back inside the panel widget, which drops the badge keys and the count).

items.title: Starters tab says 'copy one into your current sequence' but the action replaces the whole sequence
items.reasoning: Both halves are in the tree and the behaviour claim is accurate. _starters_section.dart:56-57 now reads 'Bundled, ready-to-run sample sequences. Loading one replaces your current sequence.' and :215 labels the button 'Replace with this starter'; _useStarter (:230-280) calls CurrentSequenceNotifier.loadSequence on a cloneForUse copy and only pauses on UnsavedChangesException, exactly as described. I checked the things that usually make this shape incomplete. (a) Second surface: grep for 'copy one into' / 'into your current sequence' across the repo returns only this file's explanatory comment and the test - sampleSequencesProvider has exactly one consumer (_StartersSection), so there is no second inert copy of the sentence, and the sibling Templates section header makes no copy-vs-replace claim at all. (b) Truncation, which bit the helperText item in this same shard: _TemplatesSectionHeader (templates_tab.dart:264-310) sets no maxLines and no overflow on the subtitle and it sits in an Expanded Column, so the longer honest caption wraps rather than ellipsising on a phone. (c) The button's LucideIcons.copy is not a residual untruth - the action genuinely clones the bundled starter (SampleSequenceService.cloneForUse) before loading it, so 'copy' describes what happens to the STARTER while 'replace' describes what happens to the editor. Both words are true.
items.evidence: SEVER TEST DONE: reverted the caption in _starters_section.dart to 'Tap a card to copy one into your current sequence.' and re-ran packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/starters_caption_truth_test.dart - RED on 'the Starters caption says replace, not copy-into'; restored the caption and re-ran - 2/2 green. The test pumps the real TemplatesTab with a real CurrentSequenceNotifier and its second case asserts the replace behaviour itself (name becomes the starter's, id changes), so the words cannot later be made true by weakening the behaviour they describe.
